items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 AbstractThrownPotion.onHitBlock gates on potionContents.is(Potions.WATER), direct holder equality, no tag (bytecode 55-63); onHitEntity routes water through onHitAsWater the same way (bytecode 46-59). The Rust gates all four behaviours on potion tags (game/splash_water.rs potion_in_tag :42-51; douse :60, hurt/extinguish :134-135, rehydrate :197), but 26.1 has NO potion tags beyond tradeable: PotionTags has ONLY TRADEABLE (javap-verified), the client-jar datapack and the prepared data hold only tags/potion/tradeable.json, so every gate is always false. 26.3-leak: 26.3's datapack HAS all four tag files. (26.2's tree was fixed to Potions.WATER equality; the 26.1 tree still carries the tag form.)
items.title: Splash water never douses fire, hurts, extinguishes, or rehydrates [= 1.21.7 B11-G13]

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 has 6 number providers (EnchantmentLevelProvider, ScoreboardValue, StorageValue all in the server jar). Both Rust implementations handle only 3 (constant/uniform/binomial) — enchantment_level/score/storage fall to _ => 0 (loot.rs int/float 1329-1346; items.rs number 2033-2050). Data check: 0/1326 vanilla 26.1 loot tables use the 3 missing providers. The only enchantment_level uses in 26.1 datapack (soul_speed/thorns chance) go through the separate enchant.rs random_chance path, which handles it explicitly and matches vanilla's amount.calculate(level) exactly (EnchantmentLevelProvider.getFloat javap-verified).
items.title: Three number providers return 0 (datapack-only) [= 1.21.7 B11-G12, = 26.2 B11-G02]

items.evidence: Vanilla 26.1 AnyFuel.resolve returns FuelValues.fuelItems() — the keySet of an insertion-ordered Object2IntLinkedOpenHashMap (Builder constructs one, javap-verified) populated by the hardcoded vanillaBurnTimes sequence (LAVA_BUCKET first, 20000 ticks). The Rust groups fuels by burn-time value in registry order (recipe_book.rs:566-585, native_panel_recipes.rs:173-190) — first fuel in registry order is oak planks (id 63; lava bucket 1042). items.title: Recipe-book fuel slot cycles fuels in the wrong order [= 1.21.7 B11-G15, = 26.2 B11-G03]

systemic_note: Two systemic causes recur, both worse in 26.1 than in 26.2 because the 26.1 class table carries NO dual names. (1) Class-table: 4 of 1.21.7's 9 renames carry to 26.1 with live arms dead — AbstractBed (B11-G01), RedstoneWire (B11-G02), Path (B11-G03), Speleothem (B11-G04) — all four 26.3 names present in the 26.3 jar and absent from both 26.1 jars; 26.2 had fixed RedstoneWire and Path with dual names and Speleothem was live there as PointedDripstoneBlock's parent. Group B (StrawBed, SulfurSpike, ShelfMushroom, PotentSulfur) is 26.2/26.3-only content, harmless. (2) Tags: 26.1 HAS the 26.x tags the port reads (cauldron wash, chorus, mushroom light, snow-layer, convertable_to_mud all live in 26.1 data), so most of 1.21.7's tag-degradation defects do not apply; the two exceptions are 26.3-only tags the port reads — the potion tags (B11-G05) and speleothems (second cause of B11-G04). RE-BASE WARNING: 26.1 is 26.x where 1.21.7 is not in eleven verified behaviours (trident passenger check, SwellGoal alive check, polar-bear fox age gate, lead-knot discard, mushroom/sapling bonemeal gates, golem stroll roll order, social gate, trader heightmap + SavedData storage, shipwreck heightAdjusted, players/data layout) — do not propagate 1.21.7 forms to 26.1. The 1e-5 fluid floor is present in both 26.1 vanilla (Entity constant pool) and the Rust. Two 26.1-vs-26.2 cautions: 26.1's F3 Mood literal is ONE-spaced while 26.2's is TWO-spaced, and 26.1 vanilla HAS sound variants for cows/pigs/chickens/cats (1.21.7's A02 never existed here).
